{{Portal|Mathematics}}
'''1,000,000,000,000''' ('''one trillion''' on the [[short scale]]; '''one billion''' on the [[long scale]]; one thousand [[1,000,000,000|billion]]; one million [[1,000,000|million]]) is the [[natural number]] following [[100,000,000,000#900,000,000,000 to 999,999,999,999|999,999,999,999]] and preceding 1,000,000,000,001. It is known as 10 kharab, 1000 arab, or 1 lakh crore in the [[Indian numbering system]].

== Etymology ==
The word '''trillion''' was created in the 1680s, borrowed from French ''trillion'' and Italian ''trilione'', which is from ''tri-'' ("three") + ''million'' ("a thousand thousands"). Originally in [[British English]], the word "trillion" referred to [[quintillion|million million millions]] (while "billion" referred to million millions, which is equal to trillion in [[American English]]); however, to many people, the word refers to one thousand billion (1,000,000,000,000) in the present day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Trillion - Etymology, Origin & Meaning|url=https://www.etymonline.com/word/trillion|access-date=2026-05-02 |website=etymonline|language=en-US}}</ref>

Trillion is often abbreviated as '''T''', '''t''', or '''tn'''. Rarer forms include '''tril''', '''trill''', '''tln''', and '''trn'''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Abbreviation for Trillion - Writing Explained|url=https://writingexplained.org/english-abbreviations/trillion#:~:text=The%20most%20common%20of%20which%20are%2C%20*%20T.%20*%20tn.|access-date=2026-05-02 |website=Writing Explained|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Millions, Billions, and Other Large Numbers|url=https://www.antidote.info/en/blog/reports/millions-billions-and-other-large-numbers|access-date=2026-05-02 |website=Antidote's Blog|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Properties ==
1,000,000,000,000 is written in [[scientific notation]] as '''1 × 10<sup>12</sup>''' or '''10<sup>12</sup>''' ('''1E+12''' or simply '''1E12''' in [[Scientific notation#E notation|E notation]]). It is a [[perfect power]], [[harshad number]], [[square number]] ([[1,000,000]][[Square (algebra)|<sup>2</sup>]]), [[cube number]] ([[10,000]][[Cube (algebra)|<sup>3</sup>]]), [[fourth power|tesseractic number]] ([[1000 (number)|1,000]][[fourth power|<sup>4</sup>]]), and a [[sixth power|6-hypercube number]] ([[100]][[sixth power|<sup>6</sup>]]). It is also [[Even number|even]], [[Composite number|composite]], [[Abundant number|abundant]], [[Polite number|polite]], [[Practical number|practical]], [[Frugal number|frugal]], and [[Regular number|regular]].

1,000,000,000,000 has a total of 169 [[divisor]]s (156 even, 13 odd), whose geometric mean is 1,000,000. The sum of all its divisors (including itself) is 2,499,694,822,171; therefore, its [[aliquot sum]] is 1,499,694,822,171, and its [[Abundant number|abundance]] is 499,694,822,171. All divisors are displayed below:

1,000,000,000,000 has an [[Euler's totient function|Euler totient]] of 400,000,000,000, and a [[cototient]] of 600,000,000,000. There are 37,607,912,018 positive [[prime number|prime]]s less than it.<ref name=A006880>{{Cite OEIS|A006880|Number of primes less than 10^n}}</ref>

== Scientific usage ==
For [[physical quantities]], the [[metric prefix]] '''tera-''' (symbol '''T''') indicates 1,000,000,000,000 times the base unit. For example, 10<sup>12</sup> [[bit]]s of data is called a '''terabit''', 10<sup>12</sup> [[joule]]s of energy is called a '''terajoule''', and 10<sup>12</sup> [[watt]]s of power is called a '''terawatt'''.

The computing performance of 10<sup>12</sup> [[floating point operations per second]] (teraFLOPS) is known as '''[[Computer performance by orders of magnitude#Terascale computing (1012)|terascale computing]]'''. It is the performance of several [[supercomputer]]s, such as [[NEC SX-4]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=【NEC】SX-4 |url=https://museum.ipsj.or.jp/en/computer/super/0018.html |access-date=2025-08-25 |website=IPSJ Computer Museum |publisher=[[Information Processing Society of Japan]]}}</ref> Intel's [[ASCI Red]], and [[iPhone 15 Pro]] September 2023 [[A17 Pro]] processor.

== Sense of scale ==
[[File:Visualisation_1_Trillion.svg|thumb|upright=1.8|Visualization of powers of ten from one to 10<sup>12</sup>]]
Some comparisons below give a sense of how large 1,000,000,000,000 (10<sup>12</sup>) is, according to current evidence.
=== Time ===
*10<sup>12</sup> seconds (a [[terasecond]], about 31,688 years) ago, [[homo sapiens]] were living as [[Hunter-gatherer|hunter-gatherers]].
*10<sup>12</sup> minutes (about 1.9 million years) ago, [[Homo erectus]] arose in Africa, and [[early expansions of hominins out of Africa]] started as [[archaic humans]] moved throughout Eurasia.
*10<sup>12</sup> hours (about 114 million years) ago, [[Late Cretaceous]] dinosaurs dominated the land, and [[giant squid]]s thrived in the oceans.
*10<sup>12</sup> days (about 2.74 × 10<sup>9</sup> years) ago, Earth was a world where only single-celled [[microorganism]]s existed. 10<sup>12</sup> days from now, Earth's overall surface temperature will reach {{convert| 420|K|F C}}. All life on Earth will be extinct, except single-celled microorganisms.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=O'Malley-James, Jack T. |last2=Greaves, Jane S. |last3=Raven, John A. |last4=Cockell, Charles S. |year=2012 |title=Swansong Biospheres: Refuges for life and novel microbial biospheres on terrestrial planets near the end of their habitable lifetimes |journal=International Journal of Astrobiology |volume=12 |issue=2 |pages=99–112 |arxiv=1210.5721 |bibcode=2013IJAsB..12...99O |doi=10.1017/S147355041200047X |s2cid=73722450}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Adams |first=Fred C. |author-link=Fred Adams |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-Jxc88RuJhgC&pg=PA33 |title=Global catastrophic risks |date=2008 |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |isbn=978-0-19-857050-9 |editor-last=Bostrom |editor-first=Nick |chapter=Long term astrophysical processes |editor-last2=Ćirković |editor-first2=Milan M. |editor-link2=Milan M. Ćirković|pages=33–47}}</ref>
*10<sup>12</sup> months (about 83 × 10<sup>9</sup> years) ago, the [[universe]] did not exist. 10<sup>12</sup> months from now, the Moon may collide with the Earth or be torn apart to form an orbital ring, if both have not already been destroyed.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dorminey |first=Bruce |date=31 January 2017 |title=Earth and Moon May Be on Long-Term Collision Course |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/brucedorminey/2017/01/31/earth-and-moon-may-be-on-long-term-collision-course/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170201080301/https://www.forbes.com/sites/brucedorminey/2017/01/31/earth-and-moon-may-be-on-long-term-collision-course/ |archive-date=1 February 2017 |access-date=11 February 2017 |website=Forbes}}</ref>
*10<sup>12</sup> years—a [[teraannus]]—is 70 times the [[age of the universe]]. 10<sup>12</sup> years from now, [[star formation]] may end in galaxies as they lack [[gas cloud]]s to form new stars,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Adams |first1=Fred |author-link1=Fred Adams |last2=Laughlin |first2=Greg |author-link2=Gregory P. Laughlin |year=1997 |title=A dying universe: the long-term fate and evolution of astrophysical objects |journal=Reviews of Modern Physics |volume=69 |issue=2 |pages=337–372 |arxiv=astro-ph/9701131 |bibcode=1997RvMP...69..337A |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.69.337 |s2cid=12173790}}</ref> and evidence of [[Big Bang]] may become undetectable.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Loeb |first=Abraham |year=2011 |title=Cosmology with Hypervelocity Stars |journal=Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics |publisher=Harvard University |volume=2011 |issue=4 |page=023 |arxiv=1102.0007 |bibcode=2011JCAP...04..023L |doi=10.1088/1475-7516/2011/04/023 |s2cid=118750775}}</ref>

=== Distance ===
*10<sup>12</sup> inches is about {{Convert|15|e6mile|e6km|abbr=unit}}, approximately 1/6th the distance from the Earth to the Sun.
*10<sup>12</sup> metres (a [[terametre]]) is over six times the distance from the Earth to the Sun. It is the estimated diameter of [[Betelgeuse]], a red supergiant star.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-08-09 |title=Betelgeuse: The Eventual Supernova |url=https://www.space.com/22009-betelgeuse.html |access-date=2026-07-31 |website=Space |language=en}}</ref>
*10<sup>12</sup> kilometres (a [[petametre]]) is about 1/10th a [[light-year]].

=== Area ===
*10<sup>12</sup> square inches is approximately the total area of [[Saint Lucia]], an island country in the eastern Caribbean.
*10<sup>12</sup> square feet is larger than the total area of [[Portugal]].
*10<sup>12</sup> square metres is approximately the total area of [[Ethiopia]], the 26th largest country on Earth.
*10<sup>12</sup> square kilometres is almost 2,000 times the Earth's total surface area.

=== Volume ===
*If 10<sup>12</sup> cubic metres of water were spread evenly over the Moon's surface, it would create a layer of water approximately {{convert|2.6|cm|in}} deep.
*10<sup>12</sup> grains of sand would occupy a volume of about {{convert|2|m3|ft3}}.<ref>{{cite web
 |last=Williard
 |first=David
 |title=VIMS professor authors great beach read|url=https://www.vims.edu/newsandevents/_docs/hobbs_beach_book.pdf
 |publisher=Virginia Institute of Marine Science, College of William & Mary
 |date=July 19, 2012
 |access-date=July 31, 2026
}}</ref>
